snapshot: Zyris, Inc. (Santa Barbara, CA) is a dental equipment manufacturer specializing in dental isolation technology — the Isolite System, Isolite Pro, and related products sold B2B to dental practices and clinics across North America and 20+ countries. Their IT team (Rodrigo Kammer, Director of IT; Alex Ichikawa; Rafael) manages integrations between HubSpot (CRM), Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (ERP), and Shopify (eCommerce). Current architecture is point-to-point with fragmented integrations; the goal is to centralize on MuleSoft for order-to-cash automation and internal integration ownership.
businessObjects: Products (dental equipment items — Isolite System, accessories)

phase1.label: Connected
phase1.headline: One customer record across HubSpot, D365 FO, and Shopify
phase1.body: Dental practice accounts and contacts stay synchronized across CRM, ERP, and storefront — new orders from Shopify flow into D365 FO automatically, and rep-updated pricing agreements propagate to Shopify customer tags without manual data entry.

phase2.label: Automated
phase2.headline: Order-to-cash runs without intervention
phase2.body: With connected data, FO order status updates surface in HubSpot in real time, reorder triggers fire when practices hit predictable replenishment windows, and reps see full purchase history alongside open opportunities — no tab-switching required.

phase3.label: Agentic
phase3.headline: AI that knows which practices need attention before they do
phase3.body: Unified purchase history, pricing tiers, and contact engagement data become the foundation for AI agents that surface at-risk accounts, recommend upsell timing based on equipment lifecycle, and draft follow-up sequences grounded in actual order and usage data.

p0Blockers: HubSpot connector status: SE stated no pre-built connector (Feb 2026 sales call); registry shows mule-hubspot-connector 1.0.0 — must verify operation coverage on Anypoint Exchange before architecture. If connector lacks required operations, HTTP connector + manual OAuth token subflow required (FK-005 pattern).

D365 FO PATCH not supported natively: FK-005 confirms D365 ForOperations connector does not support PATCH on OData entities. Manual HTTP fallback with OAuth token caching required for any write/update flows.

Address normalization business rules document: Zyris referenced a flowchart with address normalization logic for Shopify→FO order sync. This document was NOT included in scoping files. Required before UC2a can be architected.
D365 FO sandbox credentials: No sandbox access confirmed. Development requires either sandbox with write access or GET-only guardrail on production until UAT.
HubSpot API credentials: Private app token or OAuth 2.0 client credentials needed for development and testing.

D365 FO external ID field: A custom field must exist (or be created) in D365 FO to store HubSpot Company ID and Shopify Customer ID for deduplication — this requires FO admin action before integration development begins.

systemFindings.finding: Sam McKay (MuleSoft SE) stated 'we do not have a HubSpot connector that's pre-built' on Feb 17 2026 sales call — contradicts registry entry for mule-hubspot-connector 1.0.0. Registry entry may be community-built or have partial operation coverage. Verify on Exchange.

Client confirmed D365 Finance & Operations (FO) is the ERP. Sam McKay referenced a 'Microsoft Dynamics FO connector' exists on Anypoint Exchange. FK-005 already confirmed PATCH not supported natively for D365 FO OData entities.
Single Shopify store confirmed (no mention of multiple stores — contrast with MRN which has two). Zyris sells dental equipment via one Shopify storefront.
